jp: 冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]に{何[なに]か|ko-ka}ありますか。
en: Is there something in the fridge?
why: An unspecified thing that may exist is 何か (something); も needs a negative and でも means any.

jp: のどがかわきました。{何[なに]か|ko-ka}飲[の]みたいです。
en: I'm thirsty. I want to drink something.
why: An unnamed, unspecific thing the speaker wants is 何か (something).

jp: 玄関[げんかん]に{誰[だれ]か|ko-ka}来[き]ましたよ。
en: Someone has come to the front door.
why: An unidentified person who did something is 誰か (someone); 誰も needs a negative.

jp: 今度[こんど]の休[やす]みは、{どこか|ko-ka}へ行[い]きませんか。
en: Why don't we go somewhere during the next holiday?
why: A vague, unfixed destination (somewhere) is どこか.

jp: {いつか|ko-ka}、富士山[ふじさん]に登[のぼ]りたいです。
en: Someday I want to climb Mount Fuji.
why: An unspecified time in the future (someday) is いつか; いつも means always.

jp: 教室[きょうしつ]に{誰[だれ]か|ko-ka}いますか。電気[でんき]がついています。
en: Is someone in the classroom? The light is on.
why: Asking whether some unknown person is there is 誰か; 誰も needs a negative.

jp: {どこか|ko-ka}で財布[さいふ]を落[お]としたようです。
en: I seem to have dropped my wallet somewhere.
why: An unknown place the speaker cannot pin down is どこか (somewhere).

jp: {誰[だれ]か|ko-ka}質問[しつもん]はありますか。
en: Does anyone have a question?
why: Asking whether some person has a question is 誰か; 誰も needs a negative and 誰でも means anyone at all.

jp: 電車[でんしゃ]の中[なか]で{誰[だれ]か|ko-ka}に足[あし]を踏[ふ]まれました。
en: Someone stepped on my foot on the train.
why: An unidentified person who did the action is 誰か (someone).

jp: 暑[あつ]いですね。{何[なに]か|ko-ka}冷[つめ]たい物[もの]を飲[の]みませんか。
en: It's hot, isn't it? Shall we drink something cold?
why: Suggesting some unspecified cold thing is 何か (something).

jp: 山田[やまだ]さんは{何[なに]か|ko-ka}心配[しんぱい]しているようです。
en: Mr. Yamada seems to be worried about something.
why: A worry whose content is unknown to the speaker is 何か (something).

jp: この歌[うた]は、{どこか|ko-ka}で聞[き]いたことがあります。
en: I have heard this song somewhere.
why: A place the speaker cannot recall (somewhere) is どこか.

jp: 母[はは]は{誰[だれ]か|ko-ka}と電話[でんわ]で話[はな]しています。
en: My mother is talking on the phone with someone.
why: A person whose identity is unknown or unstated is 誰か (someone).

jp: 台所[だいどころ]から{何[なに]か|ko-ka}いいにおいがします。
en: Something smells good from the kitchen.
why: A smell of unidentified source is 何か (some / something); 何も would need a negative.

jp: {誰[だれ]か|ko-ka}、窓[まど]を開[あ]けてください。
en: Somebody, please open the window.
why: Calling out for some person to do it is 誰か (somebody); 何か would be a thing.

jp: 夏休[なつやす]みは、{どこか|ko-ka}涼[すず]しい所[ところ]へ行[い]きたいです。
en: For the summer holiday I want to go somewhere cool.
why: An as-yet-unchosen place with a described quality is どこか (somewhere).

jp: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]に{何[なに]か|ko-ka}置[お]いてあります。
en: Something has been placed on the desk.
why: An unspecified object that is there is 何か (something).

jp: 駅[えき]で{誰[だれ]か|ko-ka}が私[わたし]の名前[なまえ]を呼[よ]びました。
en: Someone called my name at the station.
why: An unknown person who did the calling is 誰か (someone).

jp: 彼[かれ]は私[わたし]に{何[なに]か|ko-ka}言[い]いたそうでした。
en: He seemed to want to say something to me.
why: Content the speaker could not tell is 何か (something).

jp: 「{何[なに]か|ko-ka}お探[さが]しですか。」と店員[てんいん]が聞[き]きました。
en: The clerk asked, "Are you looking for something?"
why: A question offering help with some unspecified item is 何か (something).

jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]は、{どこか|ko-ka}に出[で]かけますか。
en: Are you going out somewhere this weekend?
why: Asking about some unspecified place is どこか (somewhere).

jp: 今日[きょう]は忙[いそが]しくて、{何[なに]も|ko-mo}食[た]べていません。
en: I've been busy today and haven't eaten anything.
why: "Not anything" with a negative verb is 何も.

jp: 部屋[へや]には{誰[だれ]も|ko-mo}いません。
en: There is nobody in the room.
why: "Nobody" with a negative verb is 誰も.

jp: 日曜日[にちようび]は{どこへも/どこにも|ko-mo}行[い]きませんでした。
en: I didn't go anywhere on Sunday.
why: "Not anywhere" with a negative verb is どこへも (どこにも).

jp: {何[なに]も|ko-mo}わかりません。
en: I don't understand anything.
why: "Not anything" with a negative verb is 何も.

jp: 昨日[きのう]の夜[よる]は、{誰[だれ]も|ko-mo}電話[でんわ]をかけてきませんでした。
en: Last night nobody called me.
why: "Nobody" with a negative verb is 誰も.

jp: 財布[さいふ]の中[なか]には{何[なに]も|ko-mo}入[はい]っていませんでした。
en: There was nothing in the wallet.
why: "Nothing" with a negative verb is 何も.

jp: このことは{誰[だれ]にも|ko-mo}言[い]わないでください。
en: Please don't tell anyone about this.
why: "Not to anyone" with a negative request is 誰にも.

jp: 試験[しけん]が難[むずか]しくて、{誰[だれ]も|ko-mo}合格[ごうかく]できませんでした。
en: The exam was hard and nobody passed.
why: "Nobody" with a negative verb is 誰も.

jp: 夜中[よなか]の町[まち]には、{誰[だれ]も|ko-mo}歩[ある]いていませんでした。
en: There was nobody walking in the town at midnight.
why: "Nobody" with a negative verb is 誰も.

jp: 風邪[かぜ]で、{どこにも/どこへも|ko-mo}出[で]かけませんでした。
en: I had a cold, so I didn't go out anywhere.
why: "Not anywhere" with a negative verb is どこにも (どこへも).

jp: {誰[だれ]も|ko-mo}私[わたし]の話[はなし]を聞[き]いてくれません。
en: No one listens to me.
why: "No one" with a negative verb is 誰も.

jp: 疲[つか]れていて、今日[きょう]は{何[なに]も|ko-mo}したくありません。
en: I'm tired and don't want to do anything today.
why: "Not anything" with a negative form is 何も.

jp: 冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]に{何[なに]も|ko-mo}入[はい]っていないので、買[か]い物[もの]に行[い]きます。
en: There's nothing in the fridge, so I'll go shopping.
why: "Nothing" with a negative verb is 何も.

jp: 先生[せんせい]は{何[なに]も|ko-mo}おっしゃいませんでした。
en: The teacher didn't say anything.
why: "Not anything" with a negative verb is 何も.

jp: 今朝[けさ]は、{何[なに]も|ko-mo}飲[の]まずに家[いえ]を出[で]ました。
en: This morning I left home without drinking anything.
why: "Without anything" (negative ずに) is 何も.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は{何[なに]も|ko-mo}知[し]らないと言[い]いました。
en: She said she knew nothing.
why: "Knows nothing" with a negative verb is 何も.

jp: {どこも|ko-mo}空[あ]いていなくて、レストランに入[はい]れませんでした。
en: Nowhere had room, so I couldn't get into a restaurant.
why: "Nowhere" with a negative result is どこも.

jp: 山[やま]の上[うえ]は霧[きり]で、{何[なに]も|ko-mo}見[み]えませんでした。
en: The top of the mountain was foggy, and I couldn't see anything.
why: "Couldn't see anything" with a negative verb is 何も.

jp: 約束[やくそく]の時間[じかん]になっても、{誰[だれ]も|ko-mo}来[き]ませんでした。
en: Even when the appointed time came, nobody came.
why: "Nobody" with a negative verb is 誰も.

jp: 今日[きょう]は{どこにも/どこへも|ko-mo}寄[よ]らないで、まっすぐ帰[かえ]ります。
en: Today I won't stop anywhere; I'll go straight home.
why: "Not anywhere" with a negative form is どこにも (どこへも).

jp: 今[いま]、{何[なに]も|ko-mo}考[かんが]えられません。
en: I can't think about anything right now.
why: "Not anything" with a negative potential verb is 何も.

jp: 私[わたし]は肉[にく]でも魚[さかな]でも、{何[なん]でも|ko-demo}食[た]べます。
en: Whether it's meat or fish, I eat anything.
why: "Anything at all, no restriction" is 何でも.

jp: この店[みせ]では{誰[だれ]でも|ko-demo}無料[むりょう]で水[みず]が飲[の]めます。
en: At this shop anyone can drink water for free.
why: "Anyone at all" is 誰でも; 誰も cannot take an affirmative verb.

jp: 店[みせ]の前[まえ]なら、{どこでも|ko-demo}車[くるま]を止[と]めてかまいません。
en: In front of the shop you may park anywhere.
why: "Anywhere you like" is どこでも.

jp: 質問[しつもん]があれば、{いつでも|ko-demo}聞[き]いてください。
en: If you have a question, ask me any time.
why: "Any time at all" is いつでも; いつか means some day.

jp: {何[なん]でも|ko-demo}いいですから、一[ひと]つ選[えら]んでください。
en: Anything is fine, so please choose one.
why: "Anything is fine" with no restriction is 何でも.

jp: 私[わたし]のスマホは{どこでも|ko-demo}インターネットにつながります。
en: My phone connects to the internet anywhere.
why: "Anywhere at all" with an affirmative verb is どこでも.

jp: この問題[もんだい]は子[こ]どもなら{誰[だれ]でも|ko-demo}わかります。
en: Any child can understand this problem.
why: "Anyone (of the group)" with an affirmative verb is 誰でも.

jp: 駅[えき]の近[ちか]くなら、{どこでも|ko-demo}いいです。
en: Anywhere near the station is fine.
why: "Any place is fine" is どこでも.

jp: 祖父[そふ]は鳥[とり]のことなら{何[なん]でも|ko-demo}知[し]っています。
en: My grandfather knows everything there is to know about birds.
why: "Anything and everything" in an affirmative sentence is 何でも.

jp: 困[こま]ったときは、{いつでも|ko-demo}電話[でんわ]してください。
en: When you're in trouble, call me any time.
why: "At any time" is いつでも; いつか means some day.

jp: パーティーには{誰[だれ]でも|ko-demo}参加[さんか]できます。
en: Anyone can join the party.
why: "Anyone at all" with an affirmative verb is 誰でも.

jp: 子[こ]どものころは、{何[なん]でも|ko-demo}やってみたいと思[おも]っていました。
en: As a child I wanted to try anything.
why: "Anything at all" without limits is 何でも.

jp: 辞書[じしょ]があれば、{どこでも|ko-demo}勉強[べんきょう]できます。
en: As long as I have a dictionary, I can study anywhere.
why: "Anywhere at all" is どこでも.

jp: このバスに乗[の]れば、町[まち]の{どこへでも/どこにでも|ko-demo}行[い]けます。
en: If you take this bus, you can go anywhere in town.
why: "To anywhere at all" is どこへでも (どこにでも); どこへも needs a negative.

jp: 好[す]き嫌[きら]いはありません。{何[なん]でも|ko-demo}おいしく食[た]べられます。
en: I'm not picky. I can eat anything and enjoy it.
why: "Anything at all" is 何でも.

jp: あの店[みせ]の店員[てんいん]さんは、{誰[だれ]にでも|ko-demo}親切[しんせつ]です。
en: The clerks at that shop are kind to everyone.
why: "To anyone at all" is 誰にでも; 誰にも needs a negative.

jp: この薬[くすり]は{いつでも|ko-demo}飲[の]んでいいです。
en: You may take this medicine at any time.
why: "At any time" is いつでも.

jp: あの先生[せんせい]には{何[なん]でも|ko-demo}相談[そうだん]できます。
en: I can talk to that teacher about anything.
why: "About anything at all" is 何でも.

jp: 私[わたし]の犬[いぬ]は{どこでも|ko-demo}寝[ね]ます。
en: My dog sleeps anywhere.
why: "Anywhere at all" is どこでも.

jp: このクラスでは{誰[だれ]でも|ko-demo}自由[じゆう]に発言[はつげん]できます。
en: In this class anyone can speak freely.
why: "Anyone at all" with an affirmative verb is 誰でも.

jp: 赤[あか]でも青[あお]でも、{どれでも|ko-demo}いいですよ。
en: Red or blue, any of them is fine.
why: "Any one of them is fine" is どれでも いい; どれか cannot take いい this way.

jp: この果物[くだもの]は、{どこでも|ko-demo}売[う]っています。
en: This fruit is sold everywhere.
why: "Anywhere at all" with an affirmative verb is どこでも.
